title: Geometry of the qcqs finite-cover pro-etale subsite
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with its small pro-etale site $\mathcal C=X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and universes [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal D$ be the full subcategory of objects whose schemes are quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], with coverings the finite pro-etale covering families. Every affine object of $\mathcal C$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Then $\mathcal D$ is a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] with fibre products, computed as scheme fibre products, and its inclusion into $\mathcal C$ preserves fibre products and sends coverings to coverings. The slice $\mathcal D/T$ for every $T\in\mathcal D$ has finite limits computed as scheme limits over $T$, agreeing with those in $\mathcal C/T$. A finite covering in $\mathcal D$ remains a covering after adjoining any finite family of arrows with the same target. Finite disjoint unions of objects of $\mathcal D$ exist in $\mathcal D$, are the scheme disjoint unions, and are affine when all summands are affine. The topology of $\mathcal C$ is subcanonical: $h_V=\operatorname{Hom}_X(-,V)$ is a sheaf for every $V\in\mathcal C$. For every finite family $(V_i)$ in $\mathcal D$, writing $V=\coprod_i V_i$, the canonical map $\coprod_i h_{V_i}\to h_V$ is an isomorphism of sheaves of sets on $\mathcal C$, and every sheaf of sets $F$ on $\mathcal C$ satisfies $F(V)\cong\prod_i F(V_i)$, naturally in $F$. These assertions include the empty family, with $V=\varnothing$ and $F(\varnothing)$ a singleton.
